bullets.title: NVDA: Beat-and-raise expected tonight; $92.2B rev, $200B credit risk overhang in focus
bullets.body: Consensus expects NVDA to report ~$92.2B revenue (+97% YoY) with $3-4B upside vs. Street; UBS sees Oct-Q guide at ~$107-108B with stable Blackwell demand and pegs CY27/28 EPS at $15+/$20. MS flags NVDA carrying ~$200B in AI-related credit exposure by YE28 via its balance-sheet-as-a-service financing platform, introducing opaque tail risks. Hedgeye calls the print a 'nothing burger' and holds no position given 7.3% SPX weight; S&P is pricing in only 0.25% additional movement for Thursday.

bullets.title: NVDA/MRVL/AVGO: Citi raises PTs; networking seen as next AI bottleneck
bullets.body: Citi raises NVDA PT to $300 (24x F27 EPS) and MRVL PT to $275 (35x F27E) on AI DSP and optical momentum; MRVL FY27/28 EPS raised 6%/26% with Google XPO/LPU win adding socket potential. AVGO held at $500 (19x F28 EPS) with ~80bps gross margin headwind as AI ASIC mix rises from 38% to 44%. Citi identifies networking as the next primary AI bottleneck post-compute, favoring NVDA networking, AVGO, MRVL, ANET, and optical vendors.

bullets.title: MRVL: CEO bullish; 15-18 XPO designs across 4 hyperscalers, CXL a $1-1.5B opportunity
bullets.body: Marvell CEO Matt Murphy reiterates AI is in early innings with limited massive scale-up deployments. CXL memory represents $1B-1.5B opportunity addressing the AI memory wall; MRVL has 15-18 XPO designs across 4 hyperscaler clients. XPOs/ASICs will coexist with GPUs rather than replace them. CPO approaching but NPO expected to have bigger impact in next 6 months.

bullets.title: META: $18B settlement with 29 state AGs seen as manageable; stock +4.9% pre-market
bullets.body: META agreed to pay ~$18B over 10 years ($12.7B to states; $5.3B contingent on YouTube and TikTok adopting matching teen safety measures) to resolve child harm allegations — far below the feared $1.4T trial loss. META will accrue ~$10B legal charge in Q3'26 but Q3 guidance remains largely unchanged. Citi views the settlement as 'small potatoes'; shares opened +4.9% to $597.90.

bullets.title: INTU: FY27 guide disappoints at +9-10% vs. ~11% consensus; stock -10.7% pre-market
bullets.body: INTU's F4Q26 beat ($4.35B revenue, +14% YoY) was overshadowed by FY27 guide of $23.3-23.5B (+9-10%), below the ~11% Street expectation. TurboTax guided to only +2-3% YoY as price-driven churn accelerates, with GBSG 3-year growth lowered to 10-15% from 15-20%. Citi cuts PT to $416 (18x FY28 non-GAAP PE), KeyBanc cuts to $400 from $450; both maintain positive ratings. Klein/Quick Tech Bytes recommends avoiding INTU and prefers MSFT, NOW, TEAM, ORCL instead.

bullets.title: WSM: Strong 2Q beat (comps +6.2%) and raised guidance; stock -5.7% pre-market on high bar
bullets.body: WSM reported Q2 non-GAAP EPS $2.10 (cons $2.08), comps +6.2% (cons +4.5%), and raised FY26 revenue growth guidance to +4.7-7.2% (from +2.7-6.7%) with operating margin 17.8-18.2%. Broad-based outperformance across West Elm (+6.4%), Williams-Sonoma (+7.6%), and Pottery Barn (+5.1%). Stock opened -5.7% despite the beat as shares were up 30%+ YTD; Citi (Neutral, $248 PT) and UBS (Neutral, $190 PT) see stock flat-to-down; KeyBanc (Overweight, $250 PT) remains bullish.

bullets.title: ORCL: Citi opens bull catalyst watch; $330 PT; sees 4+ sigma selloff as capitulation
bullets.body: Citi's Radke opens a positive 90-day catalyst watch on ORCL after a massive 3-month selloff characterized as a 4+ standard deviation event with capitulation signals. Strong AI demand and neo-cloud pricing strength expected to support estimate revisions into the October Investor Day. PT $330 maintained.

bullets.title: MDB: DA Davidson raises PT to $465 on Atlas reaccel and AI workloads
bullets.body: DA Davidson raises MongoDB PT from $375 to $465 (Maintain Buy) expecting strong FQ2 results with Atlas growth at ~28-29% YoY vs. 26% guidance. Enterprise Advanced upside supported by Vector Search functionality. Key debate is Atlas durability and AI workload contribution. Piper Sandler maintains Overweight on MDB.

bullets.title: PANW: DA Davidson Buy, $345 PT; FQ4 expected modestly ahead but FCF margin guide may disappoint
bullets.body: DA Davidson expects PANW FQ4 to print modestly ahead on revenue/ARR metrics with FY27 guidance above on Revenue/ARR. However, FY27 Adj. FCF Margin guidance risk around 37.3% vs. ~38% Street estimate. Key debate is whether platform adoption and AI monetization (Mythos) can support durable growth reacceleration. Stock has materially outperformed into print. Piper Sandler rates PANW Overweight.

bullets.title: MU: Leadership realignment seen as positive; KeyBanc maintains OW at $1,750 PT
bullets.body: Micron promoted Manish Bhatia to President & COO and Scott DeBoer to President & CTPO; Chief Business Officer Sumit Sadana transitions to Senior Advisor. KeyBanc views the restructuring as better aligning operations with AI-driven memory demand and maintains Overweight with $1,750 PT (9x FY27 EPS of $189.62). MS cites ~18% global DRAM undersupply in 2026, forecasting DRAM prices +20-30%+ in 3Q26.

bullets.title: WDAY: F2Q27 earnings 8/27; Street watches growth recovery, AI ACV, and Silver Lake deal
bullets.body: Street expects WDAY F2Q27 revenue of $2.636B (gross margin 79.1%, op margin 30.1%, EPS $2.61). Key focus areas: revenue growth deceleration amid AI disruption, Agentic AI new ACV contribution, and any commentary on ongoing Silver Lake acquisition talks.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: Iowa AG takes Paramount/Warner merger to Supreme Court against California
bullets.body: Iowa AG filing at the Supreme Court to defend the PSKY/WBD merger against California and 12 other states seeking to block the deal, citing 68 regulator approvals globally. Iowa frames the case as an interstate commerce dispute only the Supreme Court can adjudicate, with California attempting to unilaterally regulate the transaction for the entire country.

bullets.title: AMZN: AWS acquires DuckLabs (DuckDB) to accelerate analytics capabilities
bullets.body: Amazon signed a definitive agreement to acquire DuckLabs, the Amsterdam-based developer of the DuckDB open-source analytical database, with the deal expected to close shortly. AWS and DuckLabs have collaborated since 2024; the acquisition aims to make AWS analytics faster, simpler, and more cost-effective.

bullets.title: PANW previously explored acquisitions of DDOG and OKTA; DDOG +5% on report
bullets.body: The Information reported Palo Alto Networks explored acquiring both Datadog and Okta as recently as last year before discussions ended and PANW pivoted to acquire CyberArk and Chronosphere. DDOG shares jumped ~5% in early trading on the pre-open report; OKTA little changed.

bullets.title: BABA: MiniMax raises Alibaba API and cloud spend caps dramatically through 2028
bullets.body: MiniMax increases its Alibaba API revenue cap from $0.65M to $7.5M in 2026, rising to $33M by 2028; Alibaba Cloud Services caps rise from $115M to $300M in 2026 and $500M by 2028. MiniMax plans to deploy $1.62B (80% of July fundraise) by end-2027 toward AI infrastructure and model R&D, reflecting deepening integration of Alibaba's ecosystem.

bullets.title: AMD: Confirms Zen 6 Ryzen CPU families (Olympic Ridge desktop, Medusa mobile)
bullets.body: AMD officially confirmed its Zen 6 'Ryzen' desktop CPU family codenamed Olympic Ridge (AM5 socket) and mobile families Medusa1/Medusa2 (FP10 socket). Separately, AMD Adrenalin 26.8.1 driver is causing crashes in Apex Legends on Radeon RX 9070 XT systems; a driver downgrade workaround has been recommended.

bullets.title: CRM: OpenAI sales exec Peter Doolan returning to Salesforce; enterprise AI signal
bullets.body: OpenAI's sales executive Peter Doolan is returning to Salesforce, a potential positive signal for Salesforce's enterprise AI commercial momentum and a modest negative read on OpenAI's ability to retain sales leadership. Piper Sandler rates CRM Overweight.

bullets.title: SNOW/NET/AMZN/MSFT/NFLX: Hedgeye flags as top signal strength longs
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Risk Range™ Signals model — analyzing price, volume, and volatility — identifies SNOW, NET, AMZN, MSFT, NFLX, and Unity (U) as current top-strength longs across both TRADE (3-week) and TREND (3-month+) durations.

bullets.title: INTU: OpenAI's Jalapeño ASIC delivers 1.5-1.9x better efficiency vs NVDA; AVGO/Samsung benefit
bullets.body: Per MS TMT citing SemiAnalysis, OpenAI's Jalapeño custom ASIC delivers 1.5x-1.9x more AI work per watt and 1.7x-3.6x lower latency than NVDA chips for inference workloads. SemiAnalysis sees risk to NVDA, AMD, and CBRS while AVGO, CLS, and Samsung are identified as the primary beneficiaries of the custom silicon trend.

bullets.title: NKE: Mizuho desk sees 40-60% discount to historical multiples; bullish on turnaround optionality
bullets.body: NKE is trading at 12x EV/EBITDA vs. 5-year historical 21x and 1.5x P/S vs. historical 4x after a 75% peak-to-trough decline driven by self-inflicted distribution and innovation missteps. Mizuho notes every 100bps of gross margin restored is worth ~$450-500M in annual gross profit; restoring margins from ~43% to peak ~46% would add $1.5B incrementally. Compares setup to Adidas 2013 turnaround.
